sections.text: ...SUMMARY... ISOLATED STRONG TO SEVERE GUSTS AND LARGE HAIL ARE FORECAST ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE CENTRAL AND NORTHERN GREAT PLAINS THIS EVENING. A HAIL/WIND RISK WILL BE POSSIBLE EARLY THIS EVENING IN CENTRAL NORTH CAROLINA.

sections.title: CNTRL PLAINS INTO SD
sections.text: NWLY FLOW REGIME OVER THE CNTRL U.S. WILL SERVE AS STEERING FLOW FOR WIDELY-SPACED STORM CLUSTERS TO MOVE SEWD DURING THE EVENING/OVERNIGHT. A NOTABLY DRIER BOUNDARY LAYER COMPARED TO YESTERDAY IS EVIDENT IN SURFACE OBSERVATIONS/RAOBS THIS EVENING. NONETHELESS...DEWPOINTS RANGING FROM THE 50S OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS TO THE 60S OVER THE ERN PORTIONS OF KS/NEB WILL CONTRIBUTE TO WEAK TO MODERATE BUOYANCY /500-2000 J PER KG MLCAPE/ WITHIN A FLOW REGIME SUPPORTIVE OF ORGANIZED STORM STRUCTURES. THE SEVERE THREAT THIS EVENING WILL TEND TO FOCUS NEAR STORM CLUSTERS WITH SEVERE GUSTS THE PREDOMINATE THREAT OVER THE CNTRL AND N-CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. A FAVORABLE LINEAR MODE AND STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL ACT TO HEIGHTEN THE WIND GUST THREAT IN THE NEXT FEW HOURS OVER N-CNTRL NEB AND E-CNTRL CO. A GRADUAL DIMINISHING IN STORM INTENSITY IS EXPECTED LATER THIS EVENING AND INTO THE OVERNIGHT HOURS DUE IN PART TO BOTH STABILIZATION AND FAIRLY WEAK LOW-LEVEL MASS RESPONSE. WILL MAINTAIN BROAD MARGINAL RISK OVER THE CNTRL PLAINS TO ACCOUNT FOR A CONDITIONAL...ALBEIT POORLY FOCUSED ISOLD STRONG/SEVERE THREAT DURING THE EVENING/OVERNIGHT. A WIDELY-SPACED TSTM CLUSTER OR TWO THAT MAY LINGER FROM EARLY EV

sections.title: CNTRL NC
sections.text: A WEAK DISTURBANCE MOVING ACROSS THE VA/NC VICINITY EARLY THIS EVENING WILL AID IN STORM DEVELOPMENT INTO THE MID EVENING. ADEQUATE MID-LEVEL FLOW FOR MULTICELLULAR ORGANIZATION WILL SUPPORT A HAIL/WIND THREAT FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS BEFORE THE BOUNDARY LAYER SLOWLY STABILIZES AND STORMS WEAKEN. ..SMITH.. 06/30/2016

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONVECTION WILL GRADUALLY INCREASE IN AREAL COVERAGE AND INTENSITY OVER INTO THE MID AFTERNOON HOURS. SMALL HAIL OR GUSTY WINDS CAN BE EXPECTED WITH THE STRONGEST CONVECTION.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: DIFFLUENT HIGH-LEVEL FLOW EXTENDS ACROSS NEW ENGLAND AHEAD OF MIGRATORY SHORT-WAVE TROUGH. EXTENSIVE CLOUDS WITH SCT PRECIPITATION ARE HOLDING ACROSS DOWNEAST MAINE INTO SERN CANADA WITH STRONGEST BOUNDARY-LAYER HEATING EXPECTED TO FOCUS FROM THE HUDSON VALLEY REGION OF NY...NEWD INTO EXTREME WRN MAINE. THIS CORRIDOR OF HEATING WILL BE THE PRIMARY ZONE WHERE CONVECTION COULD ATTAIN ROBUST INTENSITY. WHILE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR IS SUPPORTIVE OF ORGANIZED UPDRAFTS...INSTABILITY SHOULD REMAIN WEAK ACROSS THIS REGION AND SMALL HAIL OR GUSTY WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREATS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WIDELY SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS MAY PRODUCE PERIODIC GUSTY WINDS AND SOME SMALL HAIL THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. THE THREAT IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN MARGINAL AND A WATCH IS NOT EXPECTED AT THIS TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: WIDELY SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP ACROSS THE MCD REGION THIS AFTERNOON IN STRONG DEEP LAYER NWLY FLOW. STRONG HEATING THROUGH EARLY AFTERNOON HAS LED TO TEMPERATURES RISING INTO THE MID 70S TO MID 80S WITH DEWPOINTS GENERALLY IN THE 50S. AS A RESULT...WEAK MLCAPE NEAR 1000 J/KG WAS NOTED IN 17Z MESOANALYSIS. SOME ADDITIONAL DESTABILIZATION MAY OCCUR. THE STORMS ARE DEVELOPING ON THE FRINGES OF STRONGER EFFECTIVE SHEAR AND STEEPER MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...BUT THE ENVIRONMENT IS ADEQUATE TO SUPPORT LOOSELY ORGANIZED CELLS/CLUSTERS. STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES WITH TEMPERATURE-DEWPOINT SPREADS AROUND 20-25 DEGREES MAY ALLOW FOR PERIODIC STRONG GUSTS IN ADDITION TO SMALL HAIL IN THE STRONGER CELLS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. A WATCH MAY BE NEEDED WITHIN THE NEXT FEW HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP IN UPSLOPE FLOW NEAR HIGHER TERRAIN THIS AFTERNOON. ADDITIONAL STORMS WERE NOTED ACROSS PARTS OF SE MT ALONG AN E-W BOUNDARY IN THE VICINITY OF JDN TO MLS TO BHK. MESOANALYSIS INDICATES MAINLY UNCAPPED AIRMASS WITH MLCAPE VALUES NEAR 1000 J/KG. EFFECTIVE SHEAR GREATER THAN 40 KT SHOULD ALLOW FOR ORGANIZED STORM STRUCTURES. ADDITIONALLY...STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL SUPPORT LARGE HAIL. DAMAGING WIND GUSTS ALSO WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH DCAPE VALUES GREATER THAN 1000 J/KG AND A RELATIVELY DRY BOUNDARY LAYER WHERE DEWPOINTS WERE GENERALLY IN THE 50S...RESULTING IN TEMPERATURES-DEWPOINT SPREADS NEAR 30 DEGREES F. GIVEN THE LACK OF STRONGER DEEP LAYER FORCING AND MODEST INSTABILITY...SEVERE CONVECTION MAY REMAIN FAIRLY ISOLATED BUT TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED AND A WATCH MAY BE NEEDED AT SOME POINT THIS AFTERNOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: LARGE HAIL IS EXPECTED WITH TSTM ACTIVITY OVER THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS INTO THE EVENING HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SCT-NUMEROUS TSTMS HAVE DEVELOPED OVER THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF SRN WY/NRN CO. LEADING EDGE OF THIS ACTIVITY IS BEGINNING TO SPREAD OFF THE MOUNTAINS ALONG THE WY/CO BORDER. MRMS MESH DATA SUGGESTS SEVERE HAIL IS NOTED WITH ORGANIZING ROBUST UPDRAFT OVER WELD COUNTY. WHILE UPSLOPE FLOW IS WEAK...SUFFICIENT LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE LIKELY EXISTS FOR THIS ACTIVITY TO CONTINUE TO GROW UPSCALE AS IT SPREADS TOWARD HIGHER MOISTURE CONTENT AIR MASS OVER THE HIGH PLAINS. LARGE HAIL IS THE PRIMARY THREAT WITH SUPERCELLS ACROSS THIS REGION.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONVECTION WITH A RISK FOR SVR WIND/HAIL WILL CONTINUE SPREADING SWD/SEWD ACROSS PORTIONS OF WRN/CNTRL SD INTO THE EVENING HOURS. THIS ACTIVITY MAY SPREAD INTO PORTIONS OF SRN SD AROUND/AFTER 00Z...POTENTIALLY WARRANTING LOCAL AREAL EXTENSION OF WW 310.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AN ENE/WSW-ORIENTED QUASI-LINEAR CLUSTER OF CONVECTION IS SPREADING SWD/SEWD ACROSS PARTS OF NWRN SD. THIS ACTIVITY WILL CONTINUE ADVANCING SWD/SEWD THROUGH THE EVENING HOURS...AS INFLOW REMAINS MODERATELY UNSTABLE WITH LITTLE MLCINH. A WEAK INFLUX OF LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE FROM THE E/SE CHARACTERIZED BY DEWPOINTS IN THE LOWER/MIDDLE 50S WILL CONTINUE TO SUPPORT AROUND 1000 J/KG OF MLCAPE BEFORE NOCTURNAL COOLING PROCESSES RESULT IN DEPLETION OF BUOYANCY. WITH THE RAPID CITY VWP SAMPLING AROUND 45-55 KT OF MID-LEVEL FLOW SURMOUNTING MODEST LOW-LEVEL SELYS...DEEP SHEAR WILL REMAIN SUFFICIENT FOR SEMI-ORGANIZED CONVECTIVE STRUCTURES TO BE MAINTAINED WITH LOCALLY SVR WIND/HAIL POSSIBLE ACROSS WW 310. AFTER 00Z...THE SVR RISK COULD SPREAD S OF THE ONGOING WW BEFORE NOCTURNAL COOLING/STABILIZATION MORE SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASE. LOCAL EXTENSION OF THE WW MAY BE CONSIDERED TO ADDRESS AN ISOLATED SVR RISK SPREADING SWD/SEWD THROUGH THE EVENING HOURS. ..COHEN.. 06/29/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED STRONG TO SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT IS POSSIBLE INTO THE 00-02Z TIME FRAME. HOWEVER...THE NEED FOR A WATCH IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RELATIVELY ISOLATED BUT VIGOROUS THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS ONGOING ACROSS PARTS OF THE MID MISSOURI VALLEY...MAINLY NEAR/NORTHEAST OF THE OMAHA AREA. THIS APPEARS LARGELY IN RESPONSE TO LOCALIZED WEAKENING OF INHIBITION ASSOCIATED WITH INSOLATION...ALTHOUGH IT MAY AIDED BY WEAK LOW-LEVEL WARM ADVECTION. MID/UPPER SUPPORT FOR ACTIVITY...IF ANY...REMAINS UNCLEAR. HOWEVER...IN THE PRESENCE OF THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES CHARACTERIZED BY MODESTLY STEEP LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC LAPSE RATES AND MIXED LAYER CAPE UP TO 2000 J/KG...VERTICAL SHEAR BENEATH 25-30 KT NORTHWESTERLY 500 MB FLOW APPEARS AT LEAST MARGINALLY CONDUCIVE TO SUPERCELL STRUCTURES. AT THIS TIME...IT APPEARS THAT THERE MAY NOT BE MUCH MORE THAN AN ADDITIONAL STRONG/SEVERE STORM OR TWO THROUGH EARLY EVENING...BEFORE THE LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING CONTRIBUTES TO WANING CONVECTION. HOWEVER...IN STORMS THAT ARE ONGOING OR DO CONTINUE TO FORM UNTIL THEN...OCCASIONAL SEVERE HAIL AND LOCALIZED STRONG SURFACE GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE WEATHER THREAT FOR WW310 TO CONTINUE FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS WITH SEVERE WIND GUSTS THE MAIN THREAT AS STORMS CONGEAL INTO A SMALL FORWARD-PROPAGATING MCS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A CLUSTER OF THUNDERSTORMS RESPONSIBLE FOR SEVERE WIND GUSTS THE PAST FEW HOURS IS CURRENTLY CONGEALING INTO A SMALL FORWARD-PROPAGATING MCS. THE 40-50 KT OF EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR HAS A LARGE ORTHOGONAL COMPONENT RELATIVE TO THE EASTERN PORTION OF THE GUST FRONT AND IS PROVIDING SUSTAINED LIFT THERE ALONG THE SOUTHWARD SURGING COLD POOL. MORE DISCRETE CONVECTION IS LOCATED FARTHER BEHIND THE GUST FRONT ALONG THE WESTERN PORTION OF THE SYSTEM WHERE THE SHEAR VECTOR IS MORE PARALLEL TO THE GUST FRONT. ALTHOUGH BOTH THE BOUNDARY-LAYER AND MID-LEVEL HUMIDITY REMAIN RELATIVELY DRY...THE SYSTEM WILL SOON INGEST SLIGHTLY HIGHER LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE AS IT APPROACHES THE SOUTH DAKOTA/NEBRASKA BORDER...AND THE LIFTING ALONG WHAT IS LIKELY A DEEP COLD POOL HAS BEEN SUFFICIENT TO OVERCOME THE RELATIVELY DRY LOW-TO-MID LEVELS. LAPSE RATES ABOVE 7.5 DEG C/KM PER 00Z LBF SOUNDING AND MLCAPE AOA 1000 J/KG...WITH MUCAPE VALUES APPROACHING 2000 J/KG...SHOULD SUPPORT CONTINUED PROPAGATION OF THE MCS TO THE SOUTH-SOUTHEAST. A CONTINUATION OF THE FORWARD SPEED OF 40-45 KT WILL BRING THE GUST FRONT INTO NEBRASKA SHORTLY AFTER 01Z. AREAS S OF WW310 MAY EXPERIENCE SOME ISOLATED SVR RISK THIS EVENING...AND WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE WATCH.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A SEVERE FORWARD-PROPAGATING MCS WILL CONTINUE MOVING TO THE SOUTHEAST THROUGH NEBRASKA WITH THE THREAT FOR SEVERE WIND GUSTS CONTINUING FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS DESPITE A SLIGHT DOWNWARD TREND IN CONVECTIVE INTENSITY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: AN MCS MOVING THROUGH WW311 CONTINUES TO PRODUCE SEVERE WIND GUSTS DESPITE THE TREND TO A SLIGHTLY MORE UPSHEAR TILT AS IDENTIFIED BY AN INCREASING DISTANCE BETWEEN THE GUST FRONT AND THE CONVECTIVE LINE. SPC MESOANALYSIS FIELDS APPEARED TO BE INGESTING A SERIES OF DEWPOINT OBSERVATIONS THAT WERE TOO LOW PRIOR TO 0130Z AND SUBSEQUENTLY PRODUCING TOO LITTLE CAPE OVER NORTHERN NEBRASKA. PER LATEST OBSERVATIONS AND 00Z LBF SOUNDING...MUCAPE OF 1500-2000 J/KG LIKELY RESIDES AHEAD OF THE MCS OVER NORTHERN NEBRASKA. THIS SUFFICIENT INSTABILITY...WHEN COMBINED WITH EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 40-55 KT ORIENTED ORTHOGONALLY TO THE EASTERN PORTION OF THE COLD POOL...SHOULD ALLOW THE MCS TO MAINTAIN ITS CURRENT INTENSITY FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS. AFTER THIS TIME...NOCTURNAL COOLING OF THE NEAR-SURFACE LAYER AND THE ASSOCIATED INCREASING CONVECTIVE INHIBITION SHOULD FACILITATE A MORE SUSTAINED WEAKENING TREND. HOWEVER THE CONVECTIVE EVOLUTION WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED CLOSELY AS THE SYSTEM APPROACHES THE SOUTHERN PORTION OF THE WATCH...ESPECIALLY GIVEN THE LARGER MUCAPE OF 2000-2500 J/KG RESIDING OVER SOUTHERN NEBRASKA AND THE LATEST ESRL HRRR GUIDANCE SUGGESTING THE SYSTEM WILL REMAIN CONVECTIVELY ACTIVE FOR SEVERAL MORE HOURS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: CONTINUATION OF THE SEVERE MCS MOVING THROUGH NORTHERN NEBRASKA MAY REQUIRE THE ISSUANCE OF ANOTHER SEVERE WEATHER WATCH DOWNSTREAM OF WW 311.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A SEVERE MCS MOVING SOUTH SOUTHEAST AT 40-45 KT IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE INTO CENTRAL NEBRASKA...REACHING THE EDGE OF WW 311 BY ABOUT 0430-05Z. MEASURED SVR WIND GUSTS HAVE BEEN OBSERVED WITH THIS MCS. MODERATE INSTABILITY AND SUFFICIENT DEEP SHEAR SHOULD ALLOW FOR CONTINUATION OF STRONG CONVECTION ALONG THE LEADING EDGE OF THE COLD POOL INTO SOUTH CENTRAL NEBRASKA...WITH THE THREAT FOR AT LEAST ISOLATED SEVERE WIND GUSTS CONTINUING. HOWEVER...NOCTURNAL DECOUPLING OF THE BOUNDARY LAYER WILL TEND TO LIMIT THE OVERALL SVR RISK...CASTING UNCERTAINTY REGARDING THE NEED FOR WW ISSUANCE THOUGH TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED.
